newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan business group calls for full deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Japan business group calls for full deregulation.

text.p: Japan's biggest business group, the Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidranren), on Monday urged Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to exert strong leadership to undertake sweeping deregulation and reforms of the taxation and fiscal systems.
The request was made to Hashimoto by federation chairman Shoichiro Toyoda, a spokesman for the group said.
Hashimoto plans to finalise new steps to promote deregulation next March.

Keidanren's proposals call for the lifting or easing of 699 rules in 17 areas, with priority placed on financial business, transportation, education, welfare, employment, anti-monopoly law and telecommunications.
Keidanren urged the government to cut Japan's corporate tax rates to a level equivalent to U.S. corporate rates.
It also proposed that the government permit financial firms, now restricted to offering specific services, to enter different financial sectors.
To promote this, a ban on stock-holding companies should be lifted, it said.
